newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader orders crackdown on child sex.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader orders crackdown on child sex.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has ordered a crackdown on sexual abuse of children and an islandwide campaign to promote awareness of children's rights, a government statement said on Monday.

Kumaratunga last Friday decided to set up a Child Protection Authority and asked the Presidential Committee on Prevention of Child Abuse to draw up an action plan to deal with the sexual abuse of children and child labour, the statement said.
"The President stressed that the government would make every effort to crack down on organised criminal networks of paedophiles," it said.

The government plans to make child abuse a non-bailable offence, create desks with specially trained women officers in all police stations and set up a telephone "help line" for the public to report offences, the statement said.
The subjects of children's rights and sexually transmitted diseases also would be included in school curriculums, it said.
The move comes during growing concern over the extent of child sex abuse on the Indian Ocean island.

Last week, a Sri Lankan court sentenced a Swiss paedophile, Armin Heinrich Pfaffhauser, to two years in prison on charges of "committing an unnatural offence" for having sex with two boys in February 1995.
The case marked the first time a foreigner national was convicted for sexually abusing children in Sri Lanka, widely regarded as a popular tourist destination for the world's paedophiles.
Police have asked immigration authorities to deport 58-year-old Pfaffhauser, who pleaded not guilty during the two-year trial.
Children's rights campaigners said the sentence would have been much tougher had the suspect been tried under a new law passed in late 1995.
The new law calls for a minimum 10-year jail term and maximum 20-year sentence for pimps and their clients. It also raised the minimum age of consent to 18 for boys and 16 for girls.
Child abuse cases are pending against another Swiss national, a German and a Belgian in Sri Lankan courts. Another Swiss national, who jumped bail, is being tried in absentia.
